framework: AWS Security Best Practices + PCI-DSS v4.0
description: Comprehensive AWS Secrets Manager security checks for rotation, encryption, and access control

items.title: Secrets must not have public access via wildcard resource policy
items.description: Resource policies with Principal: '*' allow public access to secrets, exposing sensitive data.
items.remediation: Remove wildcard principals from resource policies. Use specific IAM roles/users: aws secretsmanager put-resource-policy --secret-id <ARN> --resource-policy <policy_json>

pci_dss.reason: This control requires that access to system components is denied by default. A wildcard principal (*) in a secret's resource policy grants broad access, violating the deny-by-default principle.
This control mandates that cryptographic keys are accessible only to the fewest number of custodians necessary. Public access via wildcard principals exposes encryption keys to unauthorized users.

items.title: Secrets must have automatic rotation enabled
items.description: Automatic rotation reduces the window of opportunity if credentials are compromised. Critical for database passwords, API keys.
items.remediation: Enable rotation: aws secretsmanager rotate-secret --secret-id <ARN> --rotation-lambda-arn <lambda_arn> --rotation-rules AutomaticallyAfterDays=30

pci_dss.reason: This control requires passwords/passphrases to be changed at least every 90 days for single-factor authentication. Automatic secret rotation enforces this requirement for programmatic credentials.
This control demands key-management procedures for cryptographic keys. Automatic rotation is a key management best practice to limit exposure windows.

items.title: Secrets rotation interval should not exceed 90 days
items.description: Rotation intervals >90 days increase risk of credential compromise. AWS recommends 30-90 day rotation.
items.remediation: Update rotation rules: aws secretsmanager rotate-secret --secret-id <ARN> --rotation-rules AutomaticallyAfterDays=30

pci_dss.reason: This control mandates password/passphrase changes at least every 90 days. A rotation interval exceeding 90 days fails to comply with this requirement.

items.title: Secrets should use customer-managed KMS keys for encryption
items.description: Customer-managed KMS keys provide granular control over encryption, key rotation, and access policies. AWS-managed keys limit audit visibility.
items.remediation: Create customer-managed KMS key and update secret: aws secretsmanager update-secret --secret-id <ARN> --kms-key-id <customer_key_id>

pci_dss.reason: This control requires cryptographic keys to be secured against disclosure and misuse. Customer-managed KMS keys provide enhanced control over access policies and key rotation.
This control mandates that only the fewest custodians have access to cryptographic keys. Customer-managed keys allow fine-grained IAM policies to restrict custodian access.

items.title: Secrets should not remain unrotated for more than 365 days
items.description: Secrets not rotated for 365+ days are at high risk of being compromised. Stale credentials should be rotated immediately.
items.remediation: Immediately rotate stale secrets: aws secretsmanager rotate-secret --secret-id <ARN>

pci_dss.reason: This control requires password changes at least every 90 days. A secret unrotated for 365+ days severely violates this requirement.
This control requires removing or disabling inactive accounts within 90 days. Stale secrets (>365 days) represent dormant credentials that should be rotated or removed.

items.title: Secrets should have descriptive tags for governance and cost tracking
items.description: Tags enable governance, cost allocation, and lifecycle management. Recommended tags: Environment, Owner, Purpose, CostCenter.
items.remediation: Add tags: aws secretsmanager tag-resource --secret-id <ARN> --tags Key=Environment,Value=Production Key=Owner,Value=SecurityTeam

pci_dss.reason: This control requires a data retention and disposal policy. Tags enable tracking of secret lifecycle and facilitate automated disposal based on governance policies.

items.title: Secrets should have clear descriptions documenting their purpose
items.description: Descriptions improve secret discoverability and prevent accidental deletion. Include: purpose, owning application, rotation schedule.
items.remediation: Update description: aws secretsmanager update-secret --secret-id <ARN> --description 'Production DB password for app-backend'

pci_dss.reason: This control requires documented data retention policies. Clear descriptions facilitate identification of secrets subject to retention requirements.

items.title: Critical secrets should be replicated to multiple regions for disaster recovery
items.description: Replication ensures secret availability during regional outages. Recommended for production database credentials, API keys.
items.remediation: Enable replication: aws secretsmanager replicate-secret-to-regions --secret-id <ARN> --add-replica-regions Region=us-west-2

pci_dss.reason: This control requires an incident response plan including business continuity. Secret replication ensures credential availability during regional disasters.

items.title: Secrets accessed frequently should have rotation interval less than 30 days
items.description: High-access secrets (databases, APIs) should rotate more frequently to reduce compromise window. 30-day rotation recommended.
items.remediation: For high-traffic secrets, set 30-day rotation: aws secretsmanager rotate-secret --secret-id <ARN> --rotation-rules AutomaticallyAfterDays=30

pci_dss.reason: This control mandates password changes every 90 days. For high-value secrets, a 30-day interval exceeds compliance and enhances security.

items.title: Secrets should not be accessed from Lambda functions without VPC endpoints
items.description: Lambda functions accessing secrets over public internet expose traffic to interception. Use VPC endpoints for private access.
items.remediation: Create VPC endpoint for Secrets Manager in Lambda VPC: aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint --vpc-id <vpc_id> --service-name com.amazonaws.<region>.secretsmanager

pci_dss.reason: This control requires strong cryptography for authentication credentials sent over open networks. VPC endpoints eliminate exposure to open networks.
This control mandates restricting inbound and outbound traffic to the CDE. VPC endpoints keep secret traffic within private networks.

items.title: Resource policies should require MFA for secret access
items.description: MFA prevents unauthorized access even if IAM credentials are compromised. Critical for secrets containing PII or payment data.
items.remediation: Update resource policy to require MFA: Add Condition: {'Bool': {'aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent': 'true'}}

pci_dss.reason: This control requires MFA for all access into the CDE. Secrets containing CDE data must enforce MFA via resource policies.
This control specifies MFA using two or more independent factor types. Requiring MFA in resource policies enforces this requirement.

items.title: Secrets rotation should not fail silently without alerting
items.description: Failed rotation can leave stale credentials in production. Configure CloudWatch alarms for rotation failures.
items.remediation: Create CloudWatch alarm for rotation failures: Monitor RotationSucceeded=0 metric and send SNS notification

pci_dss.reason: This control requires detection and reporting of failures of critical security systems. Rotation failures are critical security events requiring alerting.

notes: Checklist covers AWS Secrets Manager best practices with comprehensive PCI-DSS v4.0 mapping. Focuses on rotation policies (Req 8.x), encryption (Req 3.x), and access control (Req 7.x). All checks mapped to specific PCI controls with justifications.
